newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PICK SAYS CONSIDERING NEW BID FOR RINGA.
newsitem.headline: PICK SAYS CONSIDERING NEW BID FOR RINGA.

text.p: Meat processor Pick Szeged Rt said it was considering forming a consortium to bid in a second tender for one of its competitiors Ringa Husipari Rt>.

"We will think over what modifications the newly announced tender will require," Pick CEO Vilmos Bihari told Reuters in an interview. "If we go for the tender we will do it in a consortium with local pig producers."

Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt announced on Monday a new tender to sell an 85 percent stake in Ringa, based in Gyor, western Hungary, after declaring unsuccessful earlier tenders for separate stakes of 51 and 34 percent to be sold to professional investors and agricultural producers respectively.
Pick, based in Szeged, in south-east Hungary, was reported to have put in the strongest bid for the 51 percent stake while Ringa's Gyor-based pig prducers had bid for the 34 percent stake.
APV cited "production, cooperational, operational, technological and market interests reasons" for declaring the tender unsuccessful.
"APV had been concerned to save the jobs of Ringa's pig producers who feared Pick, as majority shareholder, would favour its own pig producers in Szeged," a source close to Pick told Reuters.
Bihari said Pick was now exploring involving Ringa's pig suppliers in a consortium to bid for the new tender for the whole 85 percent.

"It is not very efficient to transport the pigs from Szeged and it is important to involve the pig producers in the business," he said. "We will involve local farmers who can produce 200,000 good quality pigs per year," Bihari said.
Bihari said if a Pick-led consortium did acquire Ringa he would call an extraordinary general meeting of Pick shareholders to approve a capital increase.
Pick's annual general meeting in April rejected a plan to authorise the board to increase equity capital by up to 20 percent to pay for new acquisitions.
The board failed to win approval for the proposal from the necessary two-thirds majority, with just over 50 percent voting in favour.
Bihari told Reuters at the time he was not too disappointed as the directors had not presented any specific acquisitions plans.
This time the proposals would be specifically about Ringa. He said the anoumt of the raise would depend on the size of Pick's interest within the consortium.
"Twenty percent would be the maximum," he said.
Along with the Ringa shares, APV will also sell debts it is owed by Ringa amounting to 1.203 billion forints.
Ringa has registered capital of 824 million forints and shareholders' equity was 2.013 billion forints at the end of 1996.
Last year, the company had a pre-tax profit of 183 million forints and an operating profit of 254 million on net turnover of 15 billion last year.
Pick took over another Hungarian salami producer Herz in 1994.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pick finished steady on Wednesday at 14,500.
